annotationData and rawData directories that are stored on a network
drive. I know this will be slow but it is only for testing purposes at
the moment.

cannot get it to work:

As you can see, the paths are not correct. I believe this happens at
line 92 of findAnnotationData.R.

I have tried creating the shortcut in 2 ways, using the UNC path and
also mapping the drive and using that path, but neither works. I believe
the problem is in R.utils::filePath:

> lnk <- readWindowsShortcut("annotationData.lnk")
> pathname <- lnk$networkPathname
> pathname
[1] "\\\\eastcreek-nh\\e\\Tim\\Mike Buckley\\annotationData"
> filePath(pathname, "chipTypes")
[1] "/eastcreek-nh/e/Tim/Mike Buckley/annotationData/chipTypes"
> filePath(pathname, "chipTypes", removeUps = FALSE, expandLinks =
"none")
[1] "\\eastcreek-nh\\e\\Tim\\Mike Buckley\\annotationData/chipTypes"
> file.path(pathname, "chipTypes")
[1] "\\\\eastcreek-nh\\e\\Tim\\Mike Buckley\\annotationData/chipTypes"

As you can see, filePath is either turning the backslashes into slashes,
or removing too many slashes with removeUps = FALSE. file.path behaves
correctly in this instance, although it wont follow the shortcut to
begin with.

Also, notice on line 65 of findAnnotationData.R:

settings <- getOption("aroma.affymetrix settings");

Should be (the dot between affymetrix and settings):

settings <- getOption("aroma.affymetrix.settings");

This leads to the blank "Paths (from settings):" in the output above
(although it is an empty list on my machine anyway).

> getOption("aroma.affymetrix.settings")$annotationData$paths
list()

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

Yes, everything basically boils down to a call:

pathname <- filePath(pathname, expandLinks="any");

which parses and expands any Windows shortcut links, if detected.
filePath() is defined in R.utils. If you look at its code you'll find
that it uses readWindowsShortcut(), which is in the same package, to
actually parse the link file.

If you find a bug fix for what you describe above, I'll be happy to
add them to R.utils. The tricky thing is to make sure that it does
not break anything on other file systems/OSs.
I have not tried to use filePath()/readWindowsShortcut() for network
paths and therefore I have not tested it for that either. I can put
this on my todo list to fix it myself, but it is unlikely that it'll
make it to the top since it is not of high priority to me.

>
> Also, notice on line 65 of findAnnotationData.R:
>
> settings <- getOption("aroma.affymetrix settings");
>
> Should be (the dot between affymetrix and settings):
>
> settings <- getOption("aroma.affymetrix.settings");

Thanks for finding this one. I looked at the log files and I actually
deliberately "turned off" this feature on Feb 22, 2007, then I never
turned it back on. I cannot remember the reason, but in any case
don't try to use this settings. FYI, my strategy to provide
documentation on this project, is to put everything online. I've
started a page for "settings" in aroma.affymetrix:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/global-options

But it still has to be tuned (might rename those settings) before it
can be moved up to the user section. In any case, that page will show
the settings that you will be able to use.

Cheers

Henrik
